title: Rich Young Cluster Cep OB 3b
caption: The young star cluster Cep OB 3b, imaged by the WIYN 0.9-meter Telescope
credit: WIYN/NOIRLab/NSF/AURA/T.A. Rector (University of Alaska Anchorage) & T. Allen (University of Toledo)

recognition.text: Published in the NSF NOIRLab image archive. No published rating.

story: Cep OB 3b is a rich, young star cluster in the northern constellation Cepheus. The brightest yellow star near the centre of this image is not a member: it is a foreground star that happens to sit between us and the cluster.
The cluster's own bright stars are young and massive. They heat the surrounding gas and dust and blow out hollow cavities in the cloud.

Around these heavyweights are thousands of smaller young stars. Some of them may be in the middle of forming planetary systems. Young stars are often born surrounded by discs of gas and dust, the material from which planets can eventually assemble, so a cluster like this is a natural laboratory for studying how stars and planets begin.

understand.summary: The WIYN 0.9-meter Telescope's Mosaic camera used four filters: blue shown as blue, visual as cyan, near-infrared as orange, and a hydrogen emission line as red.
filters: 438 nm · Optical B (WIYN 0.9-meter Telescope Mosaic I)
538 nm · Optical V (WIYN 0.9-meter Telescope Mosaic I)
820 nm · Optical I (WIYN 0.9-meter Telescope Mosaic I)
657 nm · Optical Ha (WIYN 0.9-meter Telescope Mosaic I)
understand.eye: The near-infrared filter records light the eye cannot see, and the hydrogen filter isolates the glow of heated gas.
